Definition: properly, a willow twig (as pendulous), i.e. an osier; but only as woven into a basket
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says çal, it means a willow twig, woven into a basket. That is the sense that runs through its 13 occurrences, from Exodus to Genesis. The word does not change its meaning to suit the passage; the passage leans on the word.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that çal is worth knowing because God gave us the word for a willow twig, woven into a basket. The word is small; the truth it carries is not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
